title: Restore slideshow autostart after Pi relocation and reboot
description: After shutdown, relocation, and reboot on 2026-10-03, the physical Pi shows the desktop and pointer rather than the widget slideshow. User reports SSH timeout at the DHCP-reserved address. Current workstation checks reach 192.168.0.70 by ICMP and HTTP; /api/health reports piframe-office, still-photo-primary-v1, slideshow mode, clock/weather enabled, and no manifest error. Windows SSH reaches the host but rejects its changed ED25519 key; identity verification through the physical Pi is pending. Diagnose actual desktop/session, autostart launcher, browser logs, disk/power health, and SSH access, then restore slideshow startup. This worktree is a quarantined pre-history-rewrite checkout with push disabled and must not publish code.
acceptance_criteria: SSH identity is verified through a trusted channel and access is restored or a precise remaining authentication blocker is recorded. Physical Pi displays advancing slideshow plus clock/weather after restart; startup cause and repair evidence are recorded. Automatic startup is verified after a user-approved reboot. Existing pointer issue PiFrame-lh1.12 stays open until physical cursor behavior is verified.
notes:
2026-10-03 live read-only evidence: workstation LAN is 192.168.0.200; Pi reserved IP responds to ping (2/2), HTTP /api/health is healthy and identifies piframe-office, still-photo-primary-v1, slideshow, clock/weather enabled, no manifest error. Manifest contains 463 photos/slideshow items. Display config hide_cursor=true, cursor_idle_seconds=3. Windows OpenSSH reaches SSH but rejects changed host key; observed ED25519 fingerprint SHA256:BFN+ANm+jmGov30ZAbMITK04W3DgY7TKMI2otGDSzUw is UNVERIFIED. Requested hostname, hostname -I, and ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub from physical Pi. No host-key bypass or remote mutation performed. Reviewed current published kiosk-control.sh and launcher from rewritten clone remote branch; browser restart command is /opt/pi-picture-kiosk/scripts/kiosk-control.sh restart-browser in the display user's terminal. Next: verify identity, diagnose OS/session/autostart/browser logs plus storage/power before repair; retain physical restart/reboot acceptance. Existing cursor issue PiFrame-lh1.12 remains open. No repository changes.
2026-10-04 user physical evidence: running bash /opt/pi-picture-kiosk/scripts/kiosk-control.sh restart-browser restored the slideshow app with proper weather and time/date. Cursor disappearance and reboot acceptance have not been confirmed. User photo of local Pi terminal verifies hostname piframe-office, IP 192.168.0.70, and ED25519 fingerprint SHA256:BFN+ANm+jmGov30ZAbMITK04W3DgY7TKMI2otGDSzUw. Screenshot log shows October 3 16:55 backend ready and Chromium launch; later browser network-service crash/restart and Google DEPRECATED_ENDPOINT entries; 17:09:39 Gdk Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display followed by 17:09:59 Chromium exited with status 1. Thus automatic launch occurred, followed by Chromium/display-session failure; underlying protocol-error cause remains unknown. Repeated JPEG decoding warnings are present, but their timing and causal relation to browser exit are unproven. Fresh HTTP health remains healthy with slideshow, clock/weather enabled, no manifest error. Retrieved ED25519 public key independently and verified its fingerprint against physical screen. With approved escalation, backed up Windows known_hosts and replaced only stale 192.168.0.70 entries with that verified key. Default Windows SSH now passes host identity checking and reaches authentication; BatchMode fails Permission denied(publickey,password), so unattended credentials remain unavailable. Next: user password-authenticated SSH diagnostics of kiosk status/logs, labwc/user journal and power/disk state, then physical reboot acceptance or crash-recovery repair as warranted. No code changes or remote app modifications by agent.
2026-10-04 pasted password-authenticated Pi diagnostics: Debian GNU/Linux 13 trixie, Debian version 13.5. Backend ok, Chromium browser running after manual restart; GPU and renderer arguments confirm ozone-platform=wayland. Root filesystem /dev/mmcblk0p2 is 14G size, 14G used, Avail 0, Use 100%. This is a confirmed current recovery prerequisite, not proof of the cause of the earlier Wayland protocol error. vcgencmd get_throttled=0x50000 means historical undervoltage and throttling during this boot, with no active low-bit conditions at sample time; confirmed against official Raspberry Pi documentation. User journal returned no journal files/no entries, so it provides no compositor/crash evidence. cursor-helper stopped is consistent with launcher intentionally relying on app cursor hiding and does not alone establish failure; physical cursor confirmation remains pending. Need read-only disk usage breakdown and system journal/kernel evidence before selecting cleanup targets; no deletion, sync, reboot, or display-backend changes approved/performed. September 7 PiFrame-lh1.11 already records same-size root filling during legacy sync and pending deployed image-only/headroom guards. Inspect actual disk consumers and deployed sync/timer state rather than assuming recurrence. Requested current PSU/cable details. User now has interactive SSH access; agent remains without unattended credentials.
2026-10-04 next user disk breakdown: root total 14G; /srv 6.5G, /usr 4.6G, /var 2.4G, /home 191M; /srv/pi-picture-kiosk/media accounts for all 6.5G in app cache. /var listed child directories total roughly 364M (cache 139M, lib 222M, logs 836K and small others) versus 2.4G parent total: about 2G may be files directly under /var, but identity not yet established. Journals use only 8M, so journal vacuum alone will not recover meaningful headroom. systemctl is-active output in requested order: piframe-media-sync.timer active; piframe-media-sync.service failed. Need file-inclusive du for /var and bounded depth media cache totals, plus sync result/exit-status before cleanup. Timer pause would prevent further retries but has not yet been authorized; no scheduler change, deletion, or resync performed. Remains in_progress pending safe headroom recovery and startup/reboot acceptance.
2026-10-04 user confirmed video retirement/no video sync desired. Disk measurements establish photos=393M, obsolete cached videos=6.2G at exact path /srv/pi-picture-kiosk/media/media/videos, /var/swap=2.1G, active swap /dev/zram0=2G used 0B. Sync Result=exit-code and ExecMainStatus=11 (rsync file-I/O failure); full destination is consistent with failure but exact logged cause not yet read. Prepared ignored runtime recovery scripts: remove-obsolete-video-cache.sh validates exact canonical path, root-filesystem placement, and absence of mounted subtrees, stops sync timer/service, removes only that local video cache, reports free space/photos, and leaves sync paused pending photo-only verification. Bash syntax check passes. Prepared sync-from-nas-photo-only.sh from current rewritten clone origin/codex/piframe-still-ambient-widgets canonical script; supports only JPG/JPEG/PNG/WebP photos and 1GiB reserve, preserving service environment config. Bash syntax check passes. No cleanup, timer change, sync deployment, or remote mutation performed by agent: password-authenticated user execution required. Next user step: run reviewed guarded cleanup and return df plus installed script photo-only marker inspection before resuming sync. Keep photos, /var/swap, and NAS sources intact.
2026-10-04 user executed reviewed cleanup successfully: root now 7.6G used, 5.8G available, 58% used; photos remain 393M. User reports timer remains paused. Installed sync marker grep returned no lines, so installed script lacks the inspected photo-source/extension/reserve markers; do not resume that legacy script. Prepared install-photo-only-sync.sh: validates replacement SHA256, canonical installed/cache paths, root filesystem placement, no video cache, expected root-owned service ExecStart and preserved NAS/cache/credential/state environment, no unreviewed EnvironmentFile, and at least 1GiB available. Backs up previous script in private .photo-sync-backup directory, installs replacement without unit changes, runs one manual service sync, checks success/no video-cache recreation/headroom, refreshes app manifest, and restarts existing timer only after successful validation. Failure leaves timer paused. Replacement canonical photo-only script additionally rejects empty supported-photo source, enforces minimum 1GiB reserve regardless of smaller override, conservatively budgets a full incoming copy without crediting old cache, and keeps file-level rsync output in local log instead of user-visible journal. Both scripts pass Bash syntax checks. Runtime replacement SHA256 85e98a4df768120e1456c17c9df2b2d436a035693448b0427820895504d9a55e. Installer/replacement have not been deployed or executed on Pi; user interactive execution remains required. Physical reboot, stability, cursor, and power acceptance remain outstanding.
2026-10-04 physical deployment accepted at manual-sync gate: user uploaded both scripts and executed installer via password-authenticated SSH/sudo. Previous script backed up at /opt/pi-picture-kiosk/scripts/.photo-sync-backup.WWPPKR. New photo-only service reports Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0, existing timer active. No video cache recreated. Root 14G, used 7.6G, available 5.8G, 57%; photo cache now 376M. Independent current LAN API check after deployment: health ok, piframe-office, still-photo-primary-v1, mode slideshow, no manifest error; refreshed manifest contains 463 photos/slideshow items. Keep in_progress: full reboot/autostart stability, pointer, and power acceptance are still outstanding. User requested commit subject/body only; no stage, commit, branch, or push authorized. Current worktree and C:/coding/PiFrame-rewritten have empty staged/unstaged diffs and no non-ignored untracked files; diff checks pass. Recovery scripts remain ignored .runtime artifacts and are not currently committable. Draft message must explicitly be for future repository integration under PiFrame-lh1.11.2, not imply existing tracked code changes or completed reboot verification.

title: Decide whether to purge private coordinates from Git history
description: The precise weather coordinates removed under PiFrame-07k remain in commit ad7394d and in remote branch history. Decide whether the privacy benefit justifies rewriting published history. Any rewrite must be explicitly approved, backed up, coordinated with collaborators, and followed by verification across maintained branches/tags; forks and third-party caches may remain outside repository control.
acceptance_criteria: A documented decision is recorded. If approved, affected refs are identified, a backup and collaborator migration plan are reviewed, the sensitive pair is absent from all maintained published refs after the rewrite, and residual fork/cache limitations are documented. If declined, the residual exposure is explicitly accepted.
notes:
2026-09-14 decision and Gate 1: User approved rewriting published Git history to remove the private coordinate pair. Gate 1 verified a full recovery backup, excluded refs/dolt/data from the rewrite, removed the forbidden coordinate values, passed repository integrity checks, matched the expected four branch ref sets, and passed an atomic force-push dry run. First changed commit mapped 79807daa0619a1fd33ebe6785c32f3130dab5432 to 5b9f28d812106ca4d2df5469ee4ec5e276acdc07. Gate 2 was limited to atomic force-with-lease updates of refs/heads/* and refs/tags/*; git push --mirror was prohibited. 2026-09-14 Gate 2: GitHub atomically updated the four maintained branches: codex/piframe f0146812bd3b01876473763656019c2d17823eb8 -> b6280bbf538fd9e2a730a2f478afa871c6356b22; codex/piframe-still-ambient-widgets a33b92333e9b41e4e9dbd16175ad0295f9bb423c -> 35c5ff8e447cce21188c099ddee3bb7e8f44109f; codex/piframe-w-beads 21940b07fc81a843cbfa41a7c1e67bbe5fd29011 -> 348c76a0278b4bb181c17fe51524bb80c6c5e4a2; main 8ddf87ef73e307f12d90089d640be3828c92c801 -> 7acb776ad36ae5bcbe8d008e2bdfc957f0f9b6bc. Independent verification from a new isolated repository found the forbidden values absent from all published branch/tag history, confirmed the original first-changed commit is unreachable, and passed git fsck. refs/dolt/data remained unchanged during Gate 2. Existing pre-rewrite clones/worktrees remain tainted and must not push branches or tags until replaced or carefully cleaned. Residual copies in forks, cached views, pull-request refs, third-party archives, or other clones may remain outside repository control; verify GitHub fork/PR exposure and complete collaborator/local-clone migration before closing.
2026-09-14 Gate 3A verification: A fresh replacement clone at C:\coding\PiFrame-rewritten resolves main and all three maintained remote branches to the expected rewritten OIDs and passes git fsck. Its embedded Dolt database bootstrapped successfully from the GitHub Beads remote and contains PiFrame-6p4. The old shared clone at C:\coding\PiFrame and all attached worktrees are quarantined with push URL disabled://history-rewrite. Public GitHub API and remote-ref checks found zero forks, zero pull requests, zero tags, and no advertised refs/pull/* refs. GitHub or third-party caches and independent historical clones remain outside repository control. Fresh-clone local hygiene remains: restore the generated .beads/config.yaml edit, locally ignore .beads/issues.jsonl, refresh the index, and install missing Beads hooks before closure.

description: Replace private-location and region-revealing weather coordinates in tracked PiFrame configuration, README documentation, examples, and Ansible defaults with an explicitly identified public-landmark location. Verify the ignored deployment vars retain the real coordinates locally, and document that the original precise value remains in public Git history pending an explicitly approved history rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: All publishable coordinate examples and defaults use an explicitly identified public-landmark location; current tracked files contain neither the original precise private coordinates nor the former regional placeholder; README/docs direct operators to ignored vars or Ansible Vault for real coordinates; JSON, repository tests, Ansible syntax, and tracked-file scans pass; historical exposure is tracked separately without rewriting history.
notes: 2026-09-13: Replaced weather coordinates across README.md, both weather docs, tracked config/defaults, the frame vars example, and the Ansible config template with an explicitly labeled Statue of Liberty example. Confirmed ansible/group_vars/frames.yml is ignored and untracked, so its real deployment coordinates remain local and unchanged. Current tracked-file scans contain neither the original precise pair nor the former central-US placeholder. Both JSON configs parse; npm test passes 8/8; Ansible syntax check passes; git diff --check has no whitespace errors (only LF-to-CRLF notices). The original precise pair remains in public history from ad7394d and is handled by decision-gated follow-up PiFrame-6p4. Keep PiFrame-07k in progress until the sanitized change is committed and pushed.

title: Eliminate undervoltage on piframe-office
description: The September 7 recovery sync recorded repeated kernel undervoltage warnings and vcgencmd get_throttled returned 0x50000, indicating historical undervoltage and throttling. Verify the power supply, cable, and attached load before relying on unattended operation.
acceptance_criteria: After correcting the power path, reboot piframe-office and run a sustained manual or timer-driven photo sync. vcgencmd get_throttled shows no active or historical undervoltage/throttling bits for that boot, the kernel journal contains no undervoltage warning, and the result is recorded without exposing credentials or private media filenames.
notes:
2026-10-04 current user-provided diagnostics after relocation: vcgencmd get_throttled again reports 0x50000 on the present boot, meaning undervoltage and throttling have occurred since boot while neither is active at the sample instant. This refreshes physical evidence and does not prove SD corruption or Chromium-crash causation. Requested PSU voltage/current rating and cable changes after move. Keep open pending corrected power path, clean reboot flags, and sustained real-device acceptance.
User clarified current power is USB-C from a wall socket and the connection may have been unplugged or wiggled earlier. A transient loose connection is a plausible explanation for the boot's historical undervoltage flag, but supply output rating and sustained power acceptance remain unverified. Keep connection seated while diagnosing confirmed full root filesystem; do not assume hardware or storage issues resolved from current low-bit flags alone.

title: Validate synced image integrity and quarantine corrupt media
description: Some displayed images are distorted or pixelated. Determine whether source originals are damaged or copy and sync operations are corrupting them, and keep invalid media out of the display catalog.
acceptance_criteria: Sync or manifest generation validates image decodability. Invalid images are excluded from display and reported in admin. Validation records enough detail to distinguish source decode failure from copied-file mismatch where practical. Sync history shows counts of valid, skipped, and corrupt media. Documentation explains how to investigate damaged originals versus transfer problems.
notes:
Do not close until the validation and quarantine behavior has been deployed to the physical PiFrame and manually verified against representative good and damaged media, unless the user explicitly accepts local-only closure.
2026-10-04 user-provided physical Pi terminal screenshot contains repeated Chromium JPEG decode warnings: premature end of data segment, invalid SOS parameters, bad Huffman code, and extraneous bytes before markers. This is current evidence for investigating malformed images in the deployed cache, but does not distinguish damaged source originals, transfer/copy damage, or SD-card faults, and does not prove the JPEG warnings caused the Wayland/Chromium exit tracked in PiFrame-lh1.13. No media was altered or quarantined.

title: Add Ken Burns pan/zoom and refined crossfades for photo slideshow
description: Add subtle image motion and smoother transitions so the photo-first slideshow feels alive without depending on video playback.
acceptance_criteria: Slideshow supports configurable slow pan and zoom that respects image aspect ratio and avoids obvious edge exposure. Crossfades do not flash blank or white frames. Motion and transition timing remain smooth in Raspberry Pi Chromium. Admin or config can disable or tune the effect. Physical PiFrame playback is manually verified before closure.

title: Improve photo presentation and media integrity
description: Make still photos the polished center of PiFrame through refined motion, layout variation, useful context, and reliable handling of the media presented on screen.
acceptance_criteria: Photo presentation supports refined motion and transitions, optional layout variation, and album or folder context. Media-integrity work is tracked in the frame health and media ops domain so corrupt images are not presented as valid photos. Pi display behavior is verified on the physical frame before closure.

title: Add Pi-friendly still ambience scene mode
description: Replace video ambience with image-based ambient scenes that provide motion and atmosphere without requiring video decoding on the Raspberry Pi.
acceptance_criteria: Supports curated still folders such as abstract, underwater, seasonal, and fireplace-like scenes. Uses slow dissolves, subtle pan and zoom, gradient shifts, and optional lightweight canvas particles or fractal patterns. Runs smoothly in Raspberry Pi Chromium. Admin can select scene groups. No video decode path is needed for the primary ambience experience.
notes: This is the primary replacement direction for unreliable video ambience. Keep physical PiFrame deployment and manual smoothness verification as closure evidence unless the user explicitly accepts local-only closure.

title: Retire video ambience mode and movie media architecture
description: Remove or deprecate the video and movie playback paths that proved unreliable on the Raspberry Pi, making slideshow and still ambience the safe primary experience while preserving compatibility for existing configurations.
acceptance_criteria: Admin no longer presents video or movie ambience as a primary mode. Manifest and media code no longer require media/videos for the main experience. Existing configs using video or ambience degrade safely to slideshow or still ambience. Documentation explains the pivot and legacy handling. Tests or checks cover old-config compatibility and the absence of video assumptions.
notes:
Replacement candidate for PiFrame-i3x.3 and PiFrame-i3x.4. Do not close or supersede either predecessor until the replacement issues exist and the user explicitly approves supersession. Display behavior remains deployment-sensitive and requires physical PiFrame deployment and manual verification unless the user accepts local-only closure.
Local implementation completed on branch codex/piframe-still-ambient-widgets. Removed dedicated AmbienceMode and AutoMode client paths, removed video playback from SlideshowMode, changed manifest generation to index images only without requiring media/videos or allowed_video_extensions, and removed ambience/video controls and counts from admin. Added compatibility normalization so legacy ambience/auto config and runtime/API requests resolve to slideshow, with requested values and an operator warning preserved for diagnosis. Updated default/example/Ansible configs, media/NAS/kiosk docs, README, build markers, and media checks for the still-photo pivot. Retained scripts/optimize-ambience-videos.js only as a documented historical utility; it is no longer exposed as an npm workflow or used by the primary manifest. Validation: npm test passed 5 tests covering mode fallback, legacy warnings, photo-only manifest generation without a video directory, and ignored legacy video files; npm run check-media passed with the expected empty-fixture warning; node --check passed for touched JS; git diff --check passed with line-ending warnings only. Local Express smoke passed: health ok, app_build still-photo-primary-v1, no video count, no ambience manifest, POST mode=ambience returned requested ambience with effective slideshow and ambience->slideshow fallback, and admin contained no ambience mode button. Keep in_progress: changes are uncommitted/unpushed and have not been deployed to or manually verified on the physical PiFrame.
Commit 49dc110 is published on codex/piframe-still-ambient-widgets. Deployment preflight on 2026-08-22 confirmed the branch is clean and the physical target at 192.168.0.70:8080 identifies as piframe-office running the older playlist-select-v4 build. Deployment is currently blocked at SSH trust/authentication: Windows OpenSSH reports a changed ED25519 host key with fingerprint SHA256:zWjONRF0zIFSw1VixB05ZgeNxHtJSYjpK44cmCAI/Kw, while WSL reaches the host but has no non-interactive credential. PiFrame-lh1.9 is recorded as the blocker. Do not bypass host-key checking; verify the fingerprint through the physical Pi or another trusted channel before replacing the known-host entry and continuing deployment.
Physical deployment and manual acceptance completed on 2026-08-22 for commit 49dc110 on piframe-office. Deployed health reported app_build still-photo-primary-v1, mode slideshow, no manifest error, 351 photos, and image as the only media type. The deployed manifest has no video count or ambience section, and deployed admin HTML has no ambience or auto mode buttons. Live API verification requested legacy ambience and returned effective slideshow with ambience-to-slideshow fallback, then reset the runtime mode. User manually confirmed photos advance normally, transitions show no blank or white frames, clock and weather remain visible, admin slideshow controls and folder selection work, browser refresh returns to slideshow, and a full reboot automatically returns to a working slideshow. A visible pointer after reboot is separate from video-retirement acceptance and is tracked as discovered bug PiFrame-lh1.12. SSH deployment blocker PiFrame-lh1.9 was removed from this issue after deployment succeeded.
close_reason: Deployed commit 49dc110 to the physical PiFrame and manually verified photo-only slideshow, legacy mode fallback, admin controls, manifest behavior, refresh, and reboot acceptance. Post-reboot pointer visibility is tracked separately as PiFrame-lh1.12.

title: Add Pi-friendly ambience transcode workflow
description: Current ambience media includes 4K, 60fps, and very high bitrate H.264 files that play smoothly on a workstation but not through the Pi's local Chromium kiosk output. Add a repeatable workflow for producing Pi-friendly ambience copies while preserving playlist directory structure.
acceptance_criteria: A documented script or workflow can scan source ambience videos and generate optimized H.264 MP4 outputs suitable for Raspberry Pi kiosk playback. The target format is explicit, such as max 1920x1080, max 30fps, yuv420p, faststart, and a modest CRF or bitrate range. The workflow preserves abstract/underwater directory grouping, avoids overwriting source files by default, supports dry-run or report mode, and documents how to sync or select the optimized output on the PiFrame.
notes:
Implemented optimizer workflow locally. Added scripts/optimize-ambience-videos.js with dry-run report mode by default and explicit --apply output generation. The script scans a source video tree, preserves relative folders, writes to a separate destination tree by default, refuses destination paths inside/equal to source, probes with ffprobe, and transcodes only files outside the target envelope. Target defaults are H.264 MP4, max 1920x1080, max 30fps, yuv420p, CRF 23, maxrate 8000k, bufsize 16000k, faststart, audio stripped by default. Docs updated in docs/chromium-kiosk-mode.md and docs/media-layout.md with direct node commands. Validation passed: node --check, direct --help, empty sample-media dry-run, destination safety failure, npm run check-media, git diff --check with CRLF warnings only, and an ffmpeg fixture that converted a 1280x720 60fps H.264 source to H.264 yuv420p 30fps output while preserving abstract/ path. Leave open pending dry-run/apply verification against the real NAS media tree.
Post-review fixes: non-MP4 containers now force transcode instead of copy-with-.mp4-extension, standalone -- is ignored for npm forwarding, positional source/dest are accepted as fallback, and FFMPEG/FFPROBE environment values may point either to an executable or a bin directory. Final validation re-ran node --check, npm dry-run on empty sample-media, destination safety failure, npm run check-media, git diff --check, and the ffmpeg fixture producing H.264 yuv420p 30fps output.
Continued implementation: added --manifest-url support so the optimizer can read a deployed PiFrame /api/manifest and stream ambience videos over HTTP when SMB/NAS access is unavailable from the workstation. Added --limit for safe smoke tests and a --dest-required guard when using --manifest-url with --apply. ffmpeg/ffprobe child processes now clear proxy environment variables by default, with --use-proxy available if needed, because ffprobe previously tried the blocked 127.0.0.1:9 proxy path. Live validation against http://192.168.0.70:8080/api/manifest passed: one-file dry-run preserved abstract/ path, full dry-run found 52 videos with 38 transcode and 14 copy decisions, and one real --apply --limit 1 wrote .runtime/pi-optimized-videos/abstract/12251807_1920_1080_30fps.mp4 as H.264 yuv420p 1080p30 at about 8.5 Mbps. Docs now explain manifest-url mode and a videos-optimized NAS sibling workflow for testing optimized groups from admin without replacing original media. Leave open pending user review and real Pi test with optimized files selected from admin.
Reworked the intended optimizer workflow after review: manifest-url mode remains useful for diagnostics or fallback smoke tests, but the primary workflow is now workstation-to-NAS via --source plus --sibling-suffix. Example: running against office/media/videos with --sibling-suffix ' [optimized]' writes abstract [optimized] and underwater [optimized] beside the original folders, so PiFrame's existing media/videos default discovery picks them up after normal NAS sync and manifest refresh. This avoids editing the generated manifest, avoids routing full-library transcoding through the Pi HTTP server, and uses workstation resources for ffmpeg work. Added safety checks forbidding --dest with --sibling-suffix and forbidding --manifest-url with --sibling-suffix. Validation passed: sibling dry-run/apply fixture wrote abstract [optimized]/test-720p60.mp4, output probed as H.264 yuv420p 30fps, rerun skipped scanning the optimized sibling as source input, manifest fallback smoke still works, npm run check-media passed, and git diff --check passed with CRLF warnings only.
Product pivot recorded 2026-08-20: Pi-friendly transcoding is no longer the preferred product direction because the primary ambience experience is moving away from video and movie media. Replacement direction is tracked by PiFrame-i3x.5 and PiFrame-i3x.6. Keep this issue in progress; do not close or supersede it until the user explicitly approves supersession.

title: Select auto-discovered media playlists from admin
description: Directory-backed media playlists should be auto-discovered for slideshow and ambience modes, not just flattened into random media pools. Admin should show the discovered playlist/category options and allow choosing which playlist each mode cycles through at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: The manifest exposes stable playlist groups for slideshow and ambience based on configured playlist roots and immediate child directories. The runtime state can store selected slideshow and ambience playlist ids, with safe fallback when a selected playlist disappears. Slideshow and ambience playback use the selected playlist when present, otherwise all media remains available. The admin panel shows playlist selectors with media counts and can update selections without editing config files.
notes:
Local implementation complete for auto-discovered playlist selection. Manifest now exposes slideshow.groups and ambience.groups from configured playlist roots and immediate child directories. Runtime state stores slideshow_playlist_id and ambience_playlist_id through /api/mode/playlists. Admin renders slideshow/ambience playlist selectors with counts and missing-selection visibility. Kiosk slideshow and ambience modes use the selected group when present and fall back to all media if not. Validation passed: node --check on touched server/app/admin JS files, focused temp-media scan for media/photos/* and media/videos/* groups, npm run check-media, git diff --check with CRLF warnings only, modePayload selected_playlists smoke test, and local Express smoke test on PORT=18080 posting to /api/mode/playlists. Leave open pending Ansible deploy and visual/admin verification on the PiFrame.
Adjusted scanner contract so NAS playlist JSON no longer hides normal media folders. PiFrame always scans configured fallback roots such as media/photos and media/videos; synced playlist files now add extra roots instead of replacing those roots. This means a stale ambience.json listing only media/videos/abstract still results in media/videos/underwater being discovered from the default media/videos root. Bumped app_build/client build to playlist-select-v1 for deploy verification. Additional validation passed: stale ambience playlist smoke test with abstract-only JSON still discovers underwater, local Express health reports playlist-select-v1, /api/mode/playlists stores underwater selection.
Follow-up from Pi verification: deployed manifest showed duplicate ambience groups such as media/videos//underwater and media/videos/underwater because roots with trailing slashes were not canonicalized before dedupe. Fixed scanner normalization to collapse slash variants, strip trailing slashes, normalize backslashes, and reject unsafe roots. Fixed /api/mode selected_playlists normalization so old persisted values like media/videos//underwater resolve to media/videos/underwater. Reduced kiosk runtime polling from 5s to 1s so admin playlist changes apply quickly. Bumped build marker to playlist-select-v2. Validation passed: duplicate-root smoke test produces one media/videos root and no // group IDs; old double-slash runtime values normalize through modePayload and local Express POST /api/mode/playlists; node --check on touched JS; npm run check-media; git diff --check with CRLF warnings only.
Follow-up from Pi verification: manifest and admin selection were correct, but ambience playback remained on the current abstract video after selecting Underwater. Fixed AmbienceMode so runtime playlist changes reconfigure the active picker and immediately call showNext. Ambience videos no longer loop forever; they advance on natural ended events and still retain the configured max-duration timer. SlideshowMode now also applies selected playlist changes directly while active. Main runtime polling now delegates playlist updates to the active mode instead of force-restarting externally. Bumped build marker to playlist-select-v3. Validation passed: node --check for touched app/server JS, npm run check-media, git diff --check with CRLF warnings only, and local server smoke returned playlist-select-v3 with normalized playlist IDs before PowerShell job cleanup timed out.
Follow-up from Pi verification: switching from Underwater back to Abstract could leave the display on a white stage with widgets. Fixed ambience loading to keep the current playable video visible while probing the next video; a replacement layer is only shown after loadeddata/canplay or skipped after a 10s load timeout. Video load listeners are attached before calling load() to avoid missing immediate media events. This should prevent blanking the stage when an abstract clip is slow, unsupported, or otherwise fails to become playable. Build marker remains playlist-select-v4 for this deploy verification.
Additional Pi verification: the same served app is smooth when opened from the workstation at http://192.168.0.70:8080 and controlled from /admin, including dissolves and playlist transitions. Remaining visible roughness appears tied to the Pi's local kiosk/rendering path and is tracked separately in PiFrame-i3x.3.
close_reason: Completed: admin-selectable auto-discovered slideshow and ambience playlists work from the served app; remaining roughness is Pi-local rendering/playback optimization tracked in PiFrame-i3x.3.

title: Repair LightDM graphical session failure after boot
description: Physical PiFrame host boots and remains SSH reachable, and pi-picture-kiosk.service is active on port 8080, but the attached boot diagnostics show lightdm.service fails repeatedly after autologin/greeter sessions and reaches Start request repeated too quickly. The display remains at a blinking underscore instead of starting the desktop/labwc kiosk session, blocking PiFrame-lh1.5 physical cursor/startup verification.
acceptance_criteria: After reboot, lightdm.service or the chosen display/login service remains active, a graphical session starts for the desktop user, labwc or the configured desktop session is running, and the kiosk autostart can launch Chromium. Logs no longer show repeated LightDM crash loops. PiFrame-lh1.5 can resume physical cursor/startup validation.
notes:
Diagnostic attachment shows: system target is graphical.target; pi-picture-kiosk.service is active/running with Node listening on http://0.0.0.0:8080; piframe-media-sync.timer is active; no labwc/Chromium process is running; LightDM is failed after 10 restarts. Logs repeat lightdm-autologin session opened for curtis, Failed to write utmpx: No such file or directory, session closed, greeter session closes, pam_systemd release failure, LightDM GLib invalid NULL class pointer/assertion, then status=1/FAILURE. This explains blinking underscore with SSH still available. Kiosk browser log contains older Chromium failures from missing X server and prior libsqlite/NSS issue, but current boot is blocked before kiosk autostart because LightDM is down.
Follow-up repair attempt: /run/utmp and /var/run/utmp were missing; user created /run/utmp with root:utmp 0664. systemd-update-utmp.service is not present. After reset/restart, LightDM still failed after 5 restarts, but the newer 03:00 logs no longer show Failed to write utmpx. /var/log/lightdm/lightdm.log shows autologin successfully authenticates curtis, then runs /etc/X11/Xsession /usr/bin/labwc-pi; that session exits with return value 1 within ~0.4s. LightDM then tries greeter command /usr/bin/labwc -C /etc/xdg/labwc-greeter/, which also exits with return value 1 after greeter communication closes. No lightdm/labwc/wayland/Xorg/chromium/unclutter processes remain. dpkg -V shows /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf modified and libglib2.0-0 package name not installed (likely different distro package name). Next diagnostics should inspect ~/.xsession-errors, greeter logs, labwc package ownership/integrity, and session configuration.
Latest labwc diagnostics: ~/.xsession-errors shows Xsession starts for curtis, then xrdb/xhost cannot open DISPLAY and /usr/bin/unclutter reports could not open display before labwc emits only deprecation warnings. Package ownership confirms /usr/bin/labwc is package labwc and /usr/bin/labwc-pi plus /etc/xdg/labwc-greeter are rpd-wayland-core. Installed packages include rpd-wayland-core/extras, labwc, lightdm, xwayland, libglib2.0-0t64, and related GTK/Wayland packages. /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf autologins curtis to rpd-labwc and greeter-session=pi-greeter-labwc. This strongly implicates the classic X11 unclutter package/session hook as a likely labwc/Wayland startup breaker; local repo revision now stops installing unclutter by default, removes it when frame_install_unclutter is false, and prevents the launcher from starting it unless explicitly enabled. Local checks passed: git diff --check (CRLF warning only), node --check app/js/cursorIdle.js, rendered launcher bash -n. Windows PowerShell lacks ansible-playbook; WSL syntax check could not run from sandbox.
User purged package unclutter. apt reported unclutter-startup remains automatically installed and no longer required. After reset-failed/restart lightdm, lightdm still failed after 5 restarts and no lightdm/labwc/chromium/unclutter processes remained. Next step: purge/check unclutter-startup and collect fresh ~/.xsession-errors plus LightDM logs after the purge to confirm whether the Xsession unclutter error is gone or another labwc startup error remains.
User purged unclutter-startup after unclutter. Fresh .xsession-errors no longer contains /usr/bin/unclutter; only xrdb/xhost cannot open empty DISPLAY, dbus environment exports, and labwc deprecated config warnings appear before labwc-pi exits. LightDM still fails after 5 restarts: autologin command /etc/X11/Xsession /usr/bin/labwc-pi exits with return value 1 after ~0.4s, then greeter command /usr/bin/labwc -C /etc/xdg/labwc-greeter/ exits with return value 1 and empty seat0-greeter.log. This confirms unclutter was a problem but not the remaining blocker. Local repo hardening updated packages.yml to remove both unclutter and unclutter-startup when frame_install_unclutter is false and to install unclutter with install_recommends: false only when explicitly enabled. Docs now name unclutter-startup as a risky Xsession hook under labwc/Wayland. Local checks passed: git diff --check (CRLF warning only), node --check app/js/cursorIdle.js.
After purging unclutter/unclutter-startup, user reinstalled/upgraded the Raspberry Pi display stack: lightdm, lightdm-gtk-greeter, labwc, rpd-wayland-core/extras, libwlroots-0.19, libseat1, xwayland, libglib2.0-0t64, libgtk-3-0t64, plus rpd packages upgraded 1.17 -> 1.18. LightDM still failed after restart with Start request repeated too quickly and no lightdm/labwc/chromium/unclutter processes. Given prior libsqlite3 breakage that crashed sshd/Chromium NSS and now persistent LightDM/labwc failure after package reinstall, recommend clean SD card reimage and redeploy via Ansible from the hardened role that no longer installs unclutter/unclutter-startup by default and no longer forces Chromium x11.
close_reason: Validated after clean Pi reimage/redeploy: graphical session starts again, media synced on reboot, and PiFrame UI is visible enough to verify cursor behavior.

title: Repair Pi sshd libsqlite3 runtime failure
description: Physical PiFrame host accepts TCP on port 22 and the Node app is healthy, but sshd resets every SSH connection before sending its server banner. Local journal shows sshd-session fails with a symbol lookup error in /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libsqlite3.so.0. This blocks Ansible deploys and SSH-based kiosk verification.
acceptance_criteria: From the Pi itself, sudo sshd -t passes, sudo systemctl restart ssh succeeds, ssh localhost reaches authentication or logs in, and remote ssh curtis@192.168.0.70 works again. The installed libsqlite3 package is verified or reinstalled, and PiFrame-lh1.5 can resume physical kiosk validation.
notes: Remote SSH login restored after local Pi repair. User successfully connected with ssh curtis@192.168.0.70 and received the Debian login banner for piframe-office. Keep open until post-repair validation confirms sudo sshd -t passes and ssh service/socket status is healthy.
close_reason: Validated repaired on physical Pi: sudo sshd -t succeeded, ssh.service is active, ssh.socket inactive because service listener owns port 22, and remote SSH logins from 192.168.0.200 are accepted.

title: Render prioritized ops notification rail
description: Render normalized local ops notifications in an edge rail for Uptime Kuma downtime, NAS and backup failures, UPS or power events, Pi-hole or WAN problems, and general needs-attention notices.
acceptance_criteria: The widget renders urgent messages more prominently than routine messages, identifies source and severity clearly, removes expired items, and handles empty, stale, deduplicated, and offline states. Representative Kuma, NAS, backup, UPS or power, Pi-hole or WAN, and needs-attention notices are covered by fixtures or checks. The rail does not obscure primary photo or still-ambience presentation.

title: Implement ntfy notification ingest service
description: Add a backend service that reads configured ntfy topics and exposes normalized recent notifications to the widget API.
acceptance_criteria: The service can poll or stream configured ntfy topics, handles auth when configured, caches recent messages, filters by priority or tags, and returns stale/offline state without blocking the kiosk.

title: Design notification event model and source config
description: Define the normalized notification shape shared by ntfy, future Kuma status checks, frame health alerts, and display rendering.
acceptance_criteria: The design covers id, source, title, body, priority, tags, timestamps, expiry, stale behavior, dedupe keys, and display severity. Config examples cover local ntfy server URL, topics, auth, filters, and refresh settings.

title: Introduce widget registry and config model
description: Move widget startup toward a registry-driven model so new widgets can be enabled, positioned, refreshed, and tested from config without bespoke main.js wiring.
acceptance_criteria: Clock and weather continue to work through the registry model. New widget definitions include id, enabled state, position, refresh behavior, and display component wiring. Unknown or disabled widgets are ignored safely.

title: Add configurable edge rail widget zones
description: Extend the current four-corner widget layer with top, bottom, left, and right rail zones suitable for notifications and compact context widgets.
acceptance_criteria: Config supports edge rail positions. Multiple widgets in a rail stack predictably without covering core media. Responsive CSS keeps text readable at 1080p and smaller local dev windows.

title: Add local ops notification widgets
description: Bring local operations signals such as Uptime Kuma downtime, ntfy messages, NAS issues, backup alerts, and UPS notices onto the PiFrame display without disrupting slideshow or ambience playback.
acceptance_criteria: Configured local ops notifications can be ingested, cached, prioritized, and rendered on an edge area of the display. Offline or stale notification sources degrade visibly but do not block media playback.

title: Build widget platform and edge layout
description: Create the shared display and configuration foundation for more PiFrame widgets without hardcoding each one into the startup path. This should make edge rails, collision behavior, and widget previews first-class pieces of the kiosk.
acceptance_criteria: The display supports configurable corner and edge widget zones with predictable priority/collision behavior. New widgets can be registered from config without bespoke startup wiring. Admin can preview or test widget states where useful.

title: Preserve photo-only recovery safeguards in Ansible deployments
description: October 4 recovery found 6.2G obsolete video cache on a full 14G Pi filesystem with only 393M photos. Manual cache cleanup and photo-only sync succeeded. Persist supported-photo-only source/cache rules, empty-source refusal, and safe transfer headroom in canonical repository scripts and Ansible so future deploys preserve recovery. User explicitly requires C:/coding/PiFrame as the sole main working repository; do not redirect integration to additional checkouts.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical sync script and Ansible template in C:/coding/PiFrame enforce supported-image-only source/cache paths, protect a nonempty photo cache from an empty/missing source, and retain safe transfer headroom. Focused fixtures verify video exclusion, headroom failure, and empty-source preservation. Physical sync does not recreate video cache and leaves at least 1GiB available. Cache cleanup is explicit and limited to verified disposable local video files. Use the user-requested main repository C:/coding/PiFrame; any Git publication requires user approval and resolution of the existing history-rewrite push configuration.
notes:

Both systemd units carry photo subdir and reserve settings. Ansible preflight pauses loaded legacy/current sync timers and services before installation; final timer respects frame_enable_sync_timer (default true). title: Hide mouse pointer reliably after kiosk reboot
description: The mouse pointer is visible after a physical PiFrame reboot even though normal kiosk presentation is intended to remain pointer-free. Diagnose the deployed labwc/Wayland Chromium startup path and make cursor hiding reliable without depending on an unsupported X11-only helper.
acceptance_criteria: After desktop autologin and Chromium kiosk startup, the pointer is hidden during the normal slideshow without requiring manual movement or refresh. The behavior remains correct after a full physical PiFrame reboot and does not break intentional admin interaction or kiosk recovery controls. Configuration and diagnostics identify the active Wayland/X11 cursor-hiding mechanism, and physical PiFrame verification is recorded before closure.

title: Document power-loss and SD-card recovery
description: Create a repeatable recovery path for PiFrame boot failures after power loss, including reflash and redeploy guidance and resilience improvements that reduce repeat incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation covers reflash and Ansible redeploy steps, common boot failure symptoms such as missing init, filesystem errors, graphical-session failures, and a blank kiosk, and how to choose repair versus reimage. Backup and local-data assumptions are explicit. Recovery includes media resync and physical PiFrame verification. Potential resilience improvements for storage, power, filesystem behavior, and backup or restore are recorded as follow-up Beads issues when actionable.
notes: 2026-09-07 recovery evidence: piframe-office was reimaged and provisioned; the legacy whole-office sync filled the 14G root filesystem and failed with rsync code 11. The disposable cache was cleared, a controlled photo-source sync copied 463 supported images, and physical display acceptance confirmed photos plus correct clock and weather. Uncommitted worktree fixes now enforce supported-image-only sync, a 1 GiB free-space reserve, privacy-safe aggregate logs, current Debian chromium packaging, and browser log-directory creation. Local npm tests, Bash syntax checks, git diff checks, and Ansible syntax checks pass. Pending: reviewed Ansible redeploy with timer disabled, manual service sync, timer/reboot validation, and user approval for Git commit/push. Hardware undervoltage is tracked in PiFrame-lh1.11.1.

title: Add optional collage and layout variation
description: Introduce optional multi-photo arrangements and restrained layout variation so long-running slideshows do not always present one full-frame composition.
acceptance_criteria: A configurable collage or layout mode can place multiple compatible photos without unreadable cropping or overlap. Layout selection degrades safely to a single-photo view when media or viewport constraints require it. Transitions remain smooth and the feature can be disabled. Physical PiFrame presentation is manually verified before closure.

title: Investigate and improve ambience video playback smoothness
description: Ambience videos on the PiFrame can appear choppy, especially with larger 1080p/4K clips. Investigate whether this is caused by codec/profile, resolution, bitrate, Chromium hardware acceleration, Pi GPU/Wayland settings, network/sync/storage throughput, or player buffering behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The investigation identifies which video files/codecs/resolutions play smoothly on the deployed Pi and which do not. Recommendations or fixes cover encoding guidance, optional transcoding/downscaling workflow, Chromium/GPU flags where useful, and any player-side buffering or skip behavior needed to avoid visibly choppy ambience playback. Findings are documented and implementation follow-up issues are created if needed.
notes:
Created from Pi verification reports that many ambience videos play choppy. Current playlist-switching fixes do not attempt to solve playback smoothness; this task should evaluate codec/profile/resolution/bitrate, Chromium acceleration, Pi GPU/Wayland settings, and whether a local transcode/downscale workflow is needed.
New verification signal: viewing http://192.168.0.70:8080 from the workstation while controlling http://192.168.0.70:8080/admin is smooth, including dissolves and playlist transitions. The rough/choppy behavior appears specific to the Pi's local kiosk/browser output path, so investigation should focus first on Raspberry Pi Chromium rendering/GPU/video decode/compositor settings and media encoding compatibility rather than backend serving or playlist-selection logic.
Media probe from workstation via the Pi HTTP server found 52 ambience videos: 24 abstract and 28 underwater. All are H.264 High profile yuv420p, but the library is too heavy for a Pi kiosk render path: 38 are 1080p, 12 are 4K, 1 is 1440p, 13 exceed 1080p, 8 are 59.94fps plus 3 near/at 60fps, average bitrate is 18.91 Mbps, max bitrate is 65.47 Mbps, 34 exceed 10 Mbps, and 22 exceed 20 Mbps. Top risks include 4K60 underwater clips up to 65.47 Mbps and 1080p abstract clips up to 58.39 Mbps. This strongly supports a media/transcode optimization path before deeper JavaScript changes.
Product pivot recorded 2026-08-20: later real-world use concluded that videos never played successfully enough on the PiFrame, while photos work well. Replacement direction is tracked by PiFrame-i3x.5 and PiFrame-i3x.6. Keep this issue in progress; do not close or supersede it until the user explicitly approves supersession.

title: Use ambience playlist directories as separate video groups
description: Ambience mode currently plays videos, but configured subdirectories such as media/videos/abstract and media/videos/underwater are flattened into one ambience video list. This prevents the frame from treating each directory as a separate playlist/category when selecting ambience videos.
acceptance_criteria: The manifest preserves ambience playlist directory groups with stable labels and videos for each configured directory. Ambience mode selects from those groups instead of only one flattened video list, so videos under media/videos/abstract and media/videos/underwater can be treated as distinct playlists/categories. Existing flat ambience playback still works when only one directory or no explicit playlist groups are configured.
notes:
Local implementation complete for manifest/client grouping. server/mediaScanner.js now emits ambience.groups with stable path/id/label/videos and keeps ambience.videos flat for compatibility; broad ambience roots such as media/videos group videos by immediate child directory (for example abstract and underwater). app/js/ambienceMode.js now uses group-aware MediaPicker instances and falls back to the flat list if no groups exist. docs/media-layout.md and docs/synology-media-source.md document ambience directory groups. Validation passed: node --check server/mediaScanner.js, node --check app/js/ambienceMode.js, node --check app/js/mediaPicker.js, node --check app/js/main.js, npm run check-media, focused temp-media scan asserting media/videos/abstract and media/videos/underwater become separate groups, git diff --check with CRLF warnings only. Leave issue open pending deploy/visual verification on the PiFrame with real synced media.
Physical testing after the first grouping patch showed ambience still behaved as an unselectable random pool from the user's perspective. Follow-up feature PiFrame-i3x.2 was created as discovered-from this issue to expose auto-discovered slideshow and ambience playlists in admin and runtime selection.
close_reason: Completed: ambience directories are now preserved as playlist groups, deployed verification shows discovered playlists, and app-side follow-up selection work is tracked separately.

title: Improve ambience playback and playlists
description: Pivot PiFrame ambience away from unreliable movie and video playback toward Pi-friendly still-photo scenes, curated scene groups, and safe handling of legacy ambience configurations.
acceptance_criteria: Still-photo ambience is the primary scene experience and can be selected by group from admin. The main manifest and runtime do not require a video library. Legacy video and ambience configs fall back safely. Video retirement, compatibility, and still-scene performance are covered by child issues and verified on the physical PiFrame before deployment-sensitive closure.

title: Hide mouse cursor reliably on kiosk startup
description: The mouse cursor continues to show when PiFrame starts, even though the frame should work as an unattended display and not require a mouse or keyboard to be attached. Fix startup behavior so the cursor is hidden reliably while preserving ways to control, refresh, or recover the frame remotely.
acceptance_criteria: On kiosk startup, the mouse cursor is hidden without needing local mouse or keyboard input. Existing cursor hiding behavior still allows intentional control when input is available. The frame can be refreshed, reloaded, restarted, or otherwise controlled through documented SSH commands, systemd actions, scripts, or admin/API actions. Raspberry Pi deployment docs mention the preferred keyboardless control path.
notes:
Deployment-sensitive issue: do not close until physical PiFrame verification confirms startup cursor behavior and remote recovery controls. Local implementation/static checks were completed for immediate app cursor hiding, SSH control script, Ansible executable mode, docs, and launcher environment prep, but the issue remains open for real-device validation. First physical deploy failure: reboot/refresh did not hide the cursor, and kiosk-control.sh restart-browser quit Chromium but did not relaunch. Second local revision exported DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, started unclutter with explicit DISPLAY, defaulted Chromium to --ozone-platform=x11, and made restart-browser launch with the same display environment. Second physical deploy/regression report: Ansible completed successfully and sudo reboot accepted over SSH, but after reboot the frame showed on 192.168.0.70 Wi-Fi while Chromium did not auto-start; user saw maybe a localhost/taskbar flash; SSH to 192.168.0.70 was refused/reset. Follow-up diagnostics showed TCP port 22 accepted connections and Node app was healthy, but sshd reset before server banner. Blocker PiFrame-lh1.6 captured the host-level sshd/libsqlite3 failure and was closed after sudo sshd -t, active ssh.service, and successful remote SSH login validation. Third local revision after reboot/autostart regression: changed Chromium ozone handling from forced default x11 to opt-in only. Launcher now only passes --ozone-platform when frame_chromium_ozone_platform or PIFRAME_CHROMIUM_OZONE_PLATFORM is set. Example vars/docs warn x11 requires working XWayland and should stay unset if Chromium exits on startup. Local checks passed: node --check app/js/cursorIdle.js, npm run check-media, git diff --check (CRLF warning only), Git Bash syntax check for kiosk-control.sh, rendered launcher template bash -n. Ready to redeploy safer revision and verify on physical PiFrame.
Deployment attempt after SSH repair: manual ssh curtis@192.168.0.70 works, but ansible-playbook failed at Gathering Facts with Permission denied (publickey,password). Inventory only sets ansible_host and ansible_user, and playbook uses become: true; likely needs Ansible ask-pass/ask-become-pass or SSH key auth rather than indicating sshd is broken again.
Latest physical reboot symptom: after reboot the Pi shows color boot screen, Raspberry Pi OS screen, then repeated flashing underscores in the top-left before the display appears to go off/blank. User clarified SSH is available afterward, so host is still up; likely display manager/autologin/labwc/kiosk browser session issue rather than full power-off. Diagnose through SSH before further changes.
close_reason: Validated on physical PiFrame after clean reimage/redeploy: reboot synced media and kiosk startup hides the cursor without local mouse/keyboard input.

title: Add admin sync and media health history
description: Extend the LAN admin page with recent sync results, manifest freshness, media counts, and actionable stale/error indicators.
acceptance_criteria: Admin shows recent sync attempts, last successful sync, manifest age, media counts, last manifest error, and clear warnings for stale or failed states.

title: Persist NAS sync outcome history
description: Record recent sync attempts and outcomes so admin and widgets can show more than the latest timestamp.
acceptance_criteria: Sync history records start and end time, exit status, summary output or error, and retention limits. Manual and timer-driven sync paths update the same history when possible. When media validation is available, each outcome includes counts of valid, skipped, and corrupt media without exposing sensitive paths unnecessarily.

title: Build PiFrame self-health widget
description: Display concise PiFrame operational health such as backend uptime, manifest age, media counts, current mode, last sync, and stale/error status.
acceptance_criteria: The widget is optional, compact, configurable, and shows clear good/stale/error states. It reads from existing health, manifest, and runtime data where possible.

title: Add alert-aware severe weather presentation
description: Use existing NWS alert priority data to make severe weather conditions more visible when warnings or watches are active.
acceptance_criteria: Configured severe alert types can trigger a larger weather/radar presentation. Normal conditions stay compact. Test alert mode can preview the severe presentation from admin.

title: Display radar snapshots during storms
description: Implement radar as a lightweight cached snapshot shown during storms as an overlay, side panel, or periodic interlude rather than a continuously animated radar application.
acceptance_criteria: Uses the current official source and caching plan selected by PiFrame-h21.1. Radar snapshots can be enabled in config and shown during relevant weather conditions or on demand. Refresh and cache behavior handle stale or missing imagery visibly. Presentation does not permanently obscure photos or still ambience, and no heavy live animation is required.

title: Select radar display source and caching plan
description: Research current official radar sources and select a practical snapshot and caching path for PiFrame before implementation, considering sources such as official NWS or NOAA RIDGE, OGC, or MRMS products where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: The recommendation is based on current official source documentation and identifies supported URL or API patterns, licensing or usage constraints, geographic selection, refresh cadence, caching behavior, offline and stale behavior, and display fit for a Pi kiosk. It explicitly chooses a snapshot-oriented path and records why heavy live radar animation is out of scope.

title: Render today agenda widget
description: Add a display widget for today's events with compact timed and all-day presentation suitable for a wall display.
acceptance_criteria: The widget shows all-day and timed events, highlights the next event, supports privacy redaction for titles or locations, and handles empty/stale/error states without visual clutter.

title: Implement read-only Google Calendar agenda service
description: Add a backend calendar service that fetches today and near-term events from configured Google calendars with caching and stale behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The service uses read-only scopes, supports configured calendar IDs, expands recurring events for the display window, caches results, and exposes connection or refresh errors safely through an API.

title: Design Google Calendar credential and token storage
description: Define how PiFrame connects to a Google account or calendars while keeping credentials and refresh tokens out of git and out of the browser.
acceptance_criteria: The design specifies OAuth flow or token provisioning, file paths and permissions, Ansible variables or vault expectations, scopes, rotation behavior, and failure modes.

title: Document Uptime Kuma to ntfy integration
description: Document and test the recommended path for Uptime Kuma downtime and recovery alerts to appear on PiFrame through ntfy topics.
acceptance_criteria: Docs explain the Kuma notification setup, required ntfy topic conventions, priority/tag mapping, sample test alert, and expected PiFrame display behavior for down and recovered monitors.

title: Add admin widget preview controls
description: Give the LAN admin page a consistent way to preview widget states such as empty, stale, warning, and test data for supported widgets.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can trigger documented preview states for widgets that support them. Preview state is runtime-only, visible on the display, and can be reset without editing the main config.

title: Surface frame health and media ops
description: Make PiFrame's own operational state visible on the display and in admin, including backend health, manifest age, media counts, sync history, and failure signals.
acceptance_criteria: The frame exposes a concise self-health widget and richer admin details for sync/media status. Sync failures and stale media state are visible without SSHing into the Pi.

title: Add weather radar and severe mode
description: Extend the existing NWS weather widget with optional radar display and alert-aware presentation for severe weather situations.
acceptance_criteria: Weather can optionally show radar from a display-capable source, not api.weather.gov radar status endpoints. Severe alerts can trigger a larger or more prominent weather presentation. Normal weather remains compact and optional.

title: Add calendar and agenda display
description: Show useful near-term schedule context on the PiFrame, starting with a connected Google Calendar account and a privacy-aware today agenda widget.
acceptance_criteria: PiFrame can fetch read-only calendar events from configured calendars, display today's agenda without exposing unnecessary details, and report connection/refresh status in admin.

title: Add album and folder captions with future EXIF context
description: Show optional album or folder context for displayed photos and establish a safe path for later EXIF date and location metadata.
acceptance_criteria: The display can optionally show a concise album or folder caption derived from manifest context. Captions are configurable and avoid exposing unwanted path details. The data model leaves room for later EXIF capture date and location with privacy controls, stale or absent metadata handling, and no requirement to parse EXIF in the browser.

title: Enable repeatable Pi kiosk render diagnostics
description: Live Pi-local rendering diagnostics require commands on the Pi, but this Codex shell cannot SSH non-interactively because Windows OpenSSH has a stale host key and no usable key auth for the Pi. Add a repeatable diagnostic access path so future render/GPU investigations do not depend on manual password sessions.
acceptance_criteria: The repo documents or installs a reliable way to run Pi diagnostics for Chromium process flags, display mode, DRM/GPU devices, video decode tooling, and kiosk logs. The approach handles host-key refresh after SD-card reflashes and supports non-interactive or clearly guided SSH/Ansible execution from the workstation.

title: Install durable operator command shortcuts
description: Make common PiFrame operator commands available from one canonical source instead of requiring long copied SSH command strings. The solution should work for the current deployed user and future deployments/users, with Ansible installing the scripts/aliases consistently.
acceptance_criteria: A single source of truth defines operator commands for backend restart, browser refresh/restart, status, sync, and manifest refresh. Ansible deploys the command entrypoints with executable modes and makes them available to the intended SSH user or users without depending on one person's shell history. Interactive aliases or shell functions, if added, delegate to the canonical scripts rather than duplicating command logic. Documentation shows both short on-Pi usage and equivalent one-line SSH usage.

title: Add now showing media metadata widget
description: Show lightweight context for the currently displayed slideshow image or ambience video, such as album/folder, playlist, category, and later EXIF-derived date or location.
acceptance_criteria: The display can show current media context when enabled, avoids clutter by default, handles missing metadata, and does not require rescanning media on every slide change.

title: Add sunrise sunset and moon phase widget
description: Add compact day/night context using configured frame location, including sunrise, sunset, and moon phase data.
acceptance_criteria: The widget works from latitude/longitude config, caches computed or fetched values, handles stale/offline state if an external source is used, and can be positioned like other widgets.

title: Publish frame health failures to ntfy
description: Let PiFrame publish its own health or sync failures to a configured ntfy topic so the frame participates in local ops alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Configured failure conditions can publish to ntfy with sensible rate limits and dedupe. Secrets stay out of git. Notification failures do not break media playback or sync.

title: Expose calendar connection status in admin
description: Show calendar refresh status, token health, configured calendars, and last successful update in the LAN admin page.
acceptance_criteria: Admin displays whether calendar integration is enabled, last refresh time, next refresh intent, event count, token/config errors, and stale state without exposing secrets.

title: Add ambient context extras
description: Add lower-risk contextual widgets that make the frame feel more alive, such as sunrise/sunset, moon phase, air quality or pollen, and currently displayed media context.
acceptance_criteria: Ambient widgets are optional, compact, configurable, and do not dominate the display. Each external data source has stale/offline behavior and can be disabled independently.

title: Evaluate air quality and pollen data source
description: Choose whether PiFrame should display air quality, pollen, or both, and identify a reliable source that fits local-first kiosk behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The recommendation covers source availability, API/auth requirements, refresh cadence, display value, stale behavior, and whether to implement now or defer.
